name: OPA2277UA_2K5
title: OPA277, OPA2277, OPA4277: high-precision, low-drift bipolar op amps
summary: A family of precision op amps, single (OPA277), dual (OPA2277) and quad (OPA4277), with 10 µV typical offset, ±0.1 µV/°C drift, 1 nA maximum bias current and 134 dB of open-loop gain. They run from ±2 V to ±18 V at 790 µA per amplifier, give 1 MHz gain bandwidth and 0.8 V/µs slew, are unity-gain stable and free of phase reversal. One set of limits covers supplies from ±5 V to ±15 V and temperatures from -40 °C to +85 °C. The single brings out offset-trim pins.

circuits.title: OPA277 offset voltage trim
circuits.description: Nulling the offset of the single OPA277. A 20 kΩ potentiometer sits across the two trim pins (1 and 8) with its wiper on V+. Each supply pin has 0.1 µF to ground. The range of the trim is wider than the specified offset. It is for nulling the amplifier's own offset only; the dual and quad have no trim pins.

parts.note: potentiometer; pins 1 and 2 are its ends, W its wiper

circuits.title: Second-order 50 kHz low-pass filter
circuits.description: A unity-gain multiple-feedback low-pass filter with its corner at 50 kHz and a -40 dB/decade roll-off, with gain peaking under 3 dB. The input goes through 2.25 kΩ to a node with 4 nF to ground; from that node 1.13 kΩ feeds the inverting input and 2.25 kΩ returns from the output. 1 nF joins the output to the inverting input. The non-inverting input is grounded.

circuits.title: Load cell amplifier
circuits.description: Both halves of an OPA2277 make a two-amplifier instrumentation amplifier for a bridge load cell excited from V+. Amplifier B buffers the bridge output V2 with a gain of 1 + R1/R2 (R2 to ground, R1 in feedback); amplifier A takes V1 on its non-inverting input and sums in B's output through R1 against R2 in its own feedback, so VOUT = (V1 - V2)(1 + R2/R1). The two R1 resistors match and the two R2 resistors match; their values set the gain.

parts.note: four-arm strain-gauge bridge: R-ΔR and R+ΔR arms; EXC+ and EXC- are its supply corners, V1 and V2 its outputs

circuits.title: Thermocouple 4-20 mA loop transmitter with diode cold-junction compensation
circuits.description: A type J thermocouple read by both halves of an OPA2277 wired as an instrumentation-amplifier front end (gain 1 + 2RF/R = 50, RF = 10 kΩ, R = 412 Ω) feeding the VIN+ and VIN- inputs of an XTR105 4-20 mA transmitter, which sets the loop current from its 1250 Ω RG. The op amp runs from the XTR105's 5 V regulator output (about 1 mA drawn) with its V- on the XTR105's IRET. A diode beside the thermocouple's cold junction, fed from the IR1 excitation current, forms with the 1 kΩ / 25 Ω divider the reference for amplifier B. IR2 flows into the thermocouple's negative lead and through a 50 Ω potentiometer to the reference ground. RCM, 1250 Ω with 0.01 µF across it, joins this reference ground to IRET. An external NPN carries the loop current between the XTR105's V+ and IO pins; a capacitor sits across the loop terminals.

circuits.title: EMIRR IN+ test configuration
circuits.description: How EMIRR IN+ is measured: an RF source (0 V dc bias, unmodulated carrier, 201-point logarithmic sweep) drives the non-inverting input through a 50 Ω transmission line. The amplifier is a unity-gain buffer; its output passes a low-pass filter to a digital multimeter that samples and averages the dc offset. Ambient is 25 °C; the supplies are decoupled with 0.1 µF and 10 µF.

operation.text: OPA277 is one amplifier, OPA2277 two and OPA4277 four, each built with fully separate circuits so the channels do not interact, even when one is overloaded. Only the single has offset-trim pins. The OPAx277 replaces the OP-07, OP-77 and OP-177; next to the OP-177 it has lower noise, wider output swing, twice the speed and half the supply current. Enhanced-product versions OPA2277-EP and OPA4277-EP and a space version OPA4277-SP also exist.

Offset, drift, PSRR, bias current, offset current and CMRR limits differ between the P/U, PA/UA and AIDRM (VSON) order codes. Example at 25 °C: offset is ±20 µV max for OPA277P/U, ±25 µV for OPA2277P/U, ±50 µV for PA/UA and ±100 µV for AIDRM.

The part has one operating mode and works whenever the total supply is 4 V (±2 V) or more, up to 36 V (±18 V); more than 36 V can damage it. One set of limits covers the whole span from ±5 V (10 V) to ±15 V (30 V), so a design at ±10 V gets the same guaranteed figures as one at ±15 V, and the key limits also hold from -40 °C to +85 °C. Behaviour across the full ±2 V to ±18 V range is largely unchanged; what does move with supply or temperature is in the typical curves.

Stable at unity gain, with no output phase reversal and good behaviour over a wide range of loads; overshoot against load capacitance is in the typical curves. The input common-mode range ends 2 V inside each rail. The output reaches 0.5 V of V- and 1.2 V of V+ into 10 kΩ, and 1.5 V of either rail into 2 kΩ.

Each part is laser-trimmed for offset and drift, so most designs need no adjustment. The OPA277 brings out trim pins 1 and 8 for a 20 kΩ potentiometer with its wiper on V+, giving a range larger than the offset limit. Use it only to null the amplifier's own offset: trimming out offsets from elsewhere in the system adds temperature drift.

At this level of offset, thermocouple voltages at junctions of unlike metals on the input connections matter. Keep the two input junctions at the same temperature: give both input connections a similar thermal mass, keep heat sources away from the input circuit, and shield the amplifier and its inputs from moving air such as fan draughts.

Each input has a 1 kΩ series resistor and diode clamps, and the inputs survive ±30 V of differential voltage. When an input is overdriven the diodes conduct; in a unity-gain follower this can upset the slewing, without harm to the part. Any input able to go beyond a rail by over 0.7 V must have its current held to 10 mA.

An internal circuit supplies a current equal and opposite to the input transistors' base current, so the remaining bias current is small and can be of either sign. Bias current and offset current are then about the same size, so no matching resistor is wanted in the non-inverting input; adding one can increase offset and noise.

EMIRR IN+ is the rejection of RF applied to the non-inverting input, expressed in dB of offset shift caused by rectification; the inputs are the pins most sensitive to RF, the two inputs behave alike, and the non-inverting pin can be isolated for test. The dual and quad perform close to the single. Below about 1 MHz, the unity-gain bandwidth, interference falls inside the amplifier's passband.

Put a 0.1 µF low-ESR ceramic capacitor from each supply pin to ground, as close to the part as possible; a single-supply design needs only the one from V+ to ground. Noisy or high-impedance supplies make this more important.

Use a ground plane, keep analog and digital grounds apart and watch where ground current flows. Route the input traces short and away from supply and output traces, crossing noisy traces at right angles if they must cross. Place the feedback and gain resistors close to the inverting input to keep parasitic capacitance low. A low-impedance driven guard ring round critical traces cuts leakage. Clean the board after assembly; after any aqueous wash, bake it, 30 minutes at 85 °C usually being enough, to drive moisture out of the plastic package.

The DRM package is a leadless 4 mm × 4 mm 8-pin VSON with contacts on two sides and an exposed die pad. On the OPA277 its pins match the SOIC; on the OPA2277, V+ is pin 7 and Out B pin 8, the reverse of the SOIC. The pad must connect to V- and must be soldered to a board pad even at low power: it carries heat and gives the joint its strength through temperature cycling, key-push and shear tests. Standard board assembly is used.
The 50 kHz filter example is designed for a gain of 1 V/V, a -40 dB/decade response and less than 3 dB of peaking; its response is in the curves.
